deliverables: User journeys and scoped feature list
checks: State the single primary outcome and how it will be observed.
Name primary users and map their highest-value journey from entry to completion.
Separate launch-critical features from later work; give each feature an observable acceptance check.
Record constraints, integrations, assumptions, owners, and unresolved decisions.
Record exact runtime, framework, package, browser, protocol, and hosting versions in scope.
Verify every version-sensitive claim against the relevant official documentation and release notes.
Run the proposed syntax and behavior in the actual target environment; record commands and results.
Do not treat this offline tool's catalog or heuristics as current documentation research.
Tie the visual concept to audience, product character, and content rather than a generic preset.
Define semantic color roles, readable type scales, spacing rhythm, and component states.
Check contrast, focus visibility, reduced motion, and narrow-screen composition with people and tools.
Treat the selected profile as a starting point; replace it with approved brand tokens when available.
Exercise narrow, wide, zoomed, and content-heavy viewports; avoid fixed-width clipping.
Verify focus styles, reduced-motion behavior, logical reading order, and text resizing.
Check layout containment and image sizing at the actual supported browser widths.
Use landmarks, headings, labels, and native controls for their intended meaning.
Verify document language, title, description, metadata, form labels, and media alternatives.
Resolve local URLs and fragments; validate rendered behavior in target browsers.
Keep UI state and asynchronous flows explicit; provide loading, success, and failure behavior.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks and dynamic-code execution; validate untrusted data at boundaries.
Test keyboard interaction, storage privacy, error recovery, and performance on representative devices.

deliverables: Framework fit and migration decision record
Routing, rendering, data, and deployment questions
checks: Confirm framework and version from the project, not from assumptions or this static catalog.
Choose routing, rendering, state, data-fetching, and server boundaries based on requirements.
Verify official migration guidance, supported browser targets, build behavior, and hosting constraints.
Run the framework's own install, type, build, and test commands only in a trusted development environment.
Make hover-only actions available to keyboard and touch users.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion and provide a meaningful no-animation path.
Test focus, loading, disabled, success, error, and repeated-activation states.
Test all journeys with keyboard only, visible focus, zoom, and a screen reader.
Verify names, roles, values, error announcements, contrast, captions, and focus restoration.
Use automated findings as prompts for manual review; this tool does not certify WCAG conformance.
Make route labels predictable and preserve a usable back/share URL experience.
Test empty, invalid, filtered, and no-result states for search and navigation.
Check local links and fragments, active states, redirect intent, and keyboard operability.

deliverables: Roles, preview, media, and migration controls
checks: Define content models, required fields, ownership, draft and preview behavior.
Map editor roles and least-privilege publishing permissions.
Plan media accessibility, localization, backup, API, and rollback before CMS migration.
Verify CMS version, plugins, and hosting requirements against official sources.

deliverables: Catalog, cart, and order flow specification
Payment, privacy, and operational gate checklist
checks: Specify product variants, inventory, tax, shipping, promotions, refunds, and order states.
Use a compliant hosted payment provider; never store raw card data in application code or this tool.
Test idempotency, failed payments, retries, refunds, webhooks, and reconciliation in a sandbox.
Require human approval and provider-specific review before live transactions or publishing.

deliverables: Session, roles, recovery, and abuse-control requirements
checks: Select a maintained identity provider or a reviewed authentication design; never embed credentials.
Specify session rotation, logout, recovery, verification, MFA/passkeys, roles, and audit events.
Threat-model account enumeration, credential stuffing, session theft, and privilege escalation.
Test recovery and abuse controls without using real user credentials in fixtures.
Define searchable help, ticket states, service targets, escalation, and human handoff.
Map customer data fields, consent, retention, access, and deletion behavior.
Test notification delivery, duplicate messages, failures, and accessible communication alternatives.
Define request and response schemas, validation, status codes, pagination, and error shape.
Specify identity, authorization, rate limits, idempotency, timeouts, and data ownership.
Add contract, integration, failure-path, migration, and observability tests before release.
Do not run or deploy server code from this tool; review commands in the target runtime separately.

deliverables: Build, concurrency, memory, and deployment questions
checks: Record the exact requested runtime, compiler, package manager, and supported versions.
Verify language-specific behavior and dependencies in the official runtime documentation.
Design bounded concurrency, resource handling, errors, health checks, and reproducible builds.
Do not claim compilation or runtime support until the target environment has been tested.
Document each provider's owner, version, data exchanged, authentication, and failure behavior.
Set bounded timeouts, retries with backoff, rate limits, idempotency, and circuit/fallback behavior.
Keep secrets in the target platform's secret store and redact them from logs and reports.
Test contract drift, outage, duplicate delivery, and credential rotation without live side effects.

deliverables: Migration, retention, and restore verification plan
checks: Define entities, constraints, ownership, indexes, transaction boundaries, and deletion rules.
Plan backward-compatible migrations, backup verification, restore tests, and rollback limits.
Review query patterns, contention, sensitive fields, retention, and access boundaries.
Require approval before production schema or data changes.

deliverables: Queue, retry, deduplication, and backpressure checklist
checks: Specify event schema, ordering, delivery guarantee, ownership, and idempotency key.
Define retry limits, dead-letter handling, replay safety, backpressure, and retention.
Test delayed, duplicate, out-of-order, malformed, and unavailable-consumer scenarios.

deliverables: Identity, network, region, cost, and recovery questions
checks: Record availability, data location, budget, scaling, recovery, and compliance constraints.
Apply least privilege, private networking, encryption, observability, and backup controls.
Compare provider-specific services only after verifying current official docs and cost estimates.
Require explicit approval before provisioning, modifying, or deleting cloud resources.

deliverables: Domain, DNS, certificate, and CDN cutover plan
checks: Inventory current records, TTLs, ownership, redirects, certificates, and dependencies.
Prepare a staged cutover, propagation checks, origin validation, and rollback window.
Never change live DNS, certificates, or domains without owner approval and a verified recovery path.

deliverables: State, secret, policy, and rollback safeguards
checks: Pin base images and dependencies; run containers as non-root and minimize attack surface.
Protect infrastructure state, isolate environments, and keep secrets out of images and source.
Review plans and diffs before apply; protect production state and require explicit approval.
Test clean setup, health checks, rollback, and artifact provenance in the real platform.

deliverables: Staging, migration, provenance, and rollback plan
checks: Run locked, reproducible dependencies and failing tests from a clean checkout.
Add lint, type, unit, integration, security, accessibility, and build gates appropriate to the stack.
Separate preview, staging, and production credentials; review release provenance and migrations.
Require approval before production deployment and define rollback and health criteria.
Review trust boundaries, input validation, output encoding, headers, sessions, and least privilege.
Check source and configuration for secret exposure without copying secret values into reports.
Document personal-data purpose, consent, retention, access, deletion, and breach response.
Treat static findings as triage, not a penetration test or security certification.
Measure actual field and lab performance on representative devices and networks.
Review image dimensions/formats, font loading, JavaScript work, caching, and server latency.
Set and monitor performance budgets; fix the largest measured user-facing bottleneck first.
This scanner does not calculate Core Web Vitals or execute browser profiling.
Verify title, descriptions, canonical URLs, crawl rules, structured data, and redirect intent.
Test rendered pages and actual search-index behavior; static source checks are incomplete.
Use consent-aware, minimized analytics; document attribution and experiment limits.
Do not claim rankings, indexing, or analytics validity without live verification.

deliverables: Offline, update, storage, and fallback test plan
checks: Verify install metadata, icons, scope, secure-context requirements, and browser support.
Test offline routes, cache invalidation, quota exhaustion, stale data, and update recovery.
Review service-worker origin and cache boundaries; do not cache sensitive responses by default.
This tool does not emulate browser install or offline behavior.

deliverables: Desktop/mobile shell and native capability plan
Bridge, permission, signing, and release checklist
checks: Choose exact runtime and platforms; verify versions and store requirements officially.
Constrain native bridges, permissions, deep links, update channels, and packaged secrets.
Test signing, installers, device matrices, accessibility, and recovery on actual target devices.
No desktop or mobile build is performed by this static Python tool.

deliverables: Codec, bandwidth, permission, and fallback checklist
checks: Verify caption/transcript alternatives, playback controls, autoplay policy, and permission prompts.
Measure media transfer size and test bandwidth adaptation and failure fallbacks.
Test codec support and device behavior in the actual target browsers and networks.
The scanner does not decode media or initiate camera, microphone, or WebRTC access.

deliverables: Tenant, role, workflow, and data-isolation design
Billing, audit, support, and operational checklist
checks: Enforce tenant isolation at every query, cache, file, job, and administrative boundary.
Specify roles, onboarding, billing lifecycle, audit logs, support access, and data export/deletion.
Test cross-tenant access, failure handling, billing reconciliation, and restore procedures.
Require approval before live billing, account, or production-data actions.

deliverables: Content, workflow, trust, and acceptance checklist
checks: Adapt page structure, vocabulary, navigation, search, and interactions to the actual audience.
Identify domain-specific privacy, safety, moderation, transactional, and accessibility needs.
Validate claims, ownership, legal requirements, and content with accountable subject-matter reviewers.

deliverables: Translation parity and regional QA checklist
checks: Test locale routes, fallback behavior, date/number/currency formatting, and translated content parity.
Exercise right-to-left layout, bidirectional text, font coverage, and language metadata.
Review region-specific content and compliance with local experts; no legal compliance is inferred here.
Run clean install, lint, type, unit, integration, browser, mobile, and accessibility checks for the actual stack.
Include empty, extreme, repeated, delayed, offline, unauthorized, and failed-dependency cases.
Make regression checks fail on defects and rerun linked tests after the smallest repair.
This local analyzer does not run browsers, load tests, APIs, or external services.

deliverables: Service objectives, metrics, alerts, and runbook
Cost, capacity, backup, restore, and incident checklist
checks: Define user-centered SLIs/SLOs, alert owners, escalation, and incident communication.
Set cost and capacity guardrails; test backup restoration and recovery objectives.
Plan post-incident review, action ownership, retention, and failure-safe behavior.
No production metrics or provider state are accessed by this tool.

deliverables: Legacy inventory and staged migration path
URL/data preservation, regression, and rollback plan
checks: Inventory runtime versions, routes, dependencies, data ownership, integrations, and known behavior.
Preserve source, URLs, data, accessibility, and user-visible behavior through small reversible stages.
Build regression coverage and backup/rollback points before each migration step.
Require system-owner approval; this tool does not edit or migrate an existing repository automatically.

deliverables: Checked local vertical slice and staged expansion sequence
checks: Map each request to a named capability, artifact, and observable acceptance check.
Build a minimal vertical slice with supported local tools, then verify it before expansion.
Preserve passing artifacts, isolate the earliest failing layer, repair narrowly, and rerun linked checks.
Require human approval before publishing, deployment, credentials, payments, destructive edits, or privileged actions.
Use the separate scaffold and audit commands for the implemented static HTML/CSS/JavaScript path.
